title: Impact of Emissions Standard Announcement on Auto Maker Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study (market model). The announcement date (event_day = 0) is the shock. We estimate expected returns using a pre-event estimation window and compute abnormal returns (AR) and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around the event window.
- Why: We have a single treated firm (CAR) and a clearly-timed announcement. An event study isolates short-horizon stock price reactions to news by purging market-wide movements.
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding firm-specific news in the narrow event window.
  - The market model holds: E[ret_t] = alpha + beta*mkt_ret_t, with parameters estimated from a pre-event window that is not affected by the event.
  - Beta and alpha are stable between estimation and event windows; abnormal returns are i.i.d. with constant variance over short horizons.
  - Market is efficient enough that effects are reflected quickly around the event.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load and analyze: Event Study for CAR around emissions standard announcement
# Data file path: experiments/exp_b/data/s65_data.csv

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s65_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
if(!all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df))){
  stop("Required columns are missing from the input file.")
}
df$event_day <- as.integer(df$event_day)

# 2) Define windows
# Estimation window: all available pre-event days up to -6 (avoid near-event contamination)
est_win <- df$event_day <= -6
# If too few observations, fallback to all negatives
if(sum(est_win) < 10 && any(df$event_day < 0)) {
  est_win <- df$event_day < 0
}

# Event windows to evaluate
main_window <- c(-1, 1)  # Primary: [-1, +1]
alt_window1 <- c(0, 1)   # Alternative: [0, +1]
alt_window2 <- c(0, 0)   # Announcement day only
placebo_window <- c(-10, -6) # Placebo pre-event

# Helper to compute CAR stats given alpha, beta, and a sigma from estimation window
car_stats <- function(data, alpha, beta, sigma_e, window, est_df) {
  wdat <- subset(data, event_day >= window[1] & event_day <= window[2])
  k <- nrow(wdat)
  if(k == 0) {
    return(list(CAR=NA, t=NA, p=NA, k=0))
  }
  AR <- wdat$ret - (alpha + beta * wdat$mkt_ret)
  CAR <- sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE)
  # t-stat with variance k * sigma_e^2; use df from estimation (n_est - params)
  t_stat <- if(is.finite(sigma_e) && sigma_e > 0) CAR / (sqrt(k) * sigma_e) else NA
  # Two-sided p-value using t-dist with est_df degrees of freedom
  p_val <- if(is.finite(t_stat)) 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df = est_df) else NA
  list(CAR=CAR, t=t_stat, p=p_val, k=k)
}

# 3) Estimate models on the estimation window
est <- subset(df, est_win)
n_est <- nrow(est)
if(n_est < 5) stop("Insufficient pre-event observations for estimation.")

# (A) Market model: estimate alpha and beta via OLS on pre-event window
mm_fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est)
alpha_hat <- coef(mm_fit)[1]
beta_hat  <- coef(mm_fit)[2]
sigma_hat <- sqrt(sum(residuals(mm_fit)^2) / (n_est - 2))  # residual std (df-adjusted)

# (B) Market-adjusted model (MAM): alpha=0, beta=1; sigma from pre-event residuals
mam_resid <- est$ret - est$mkt_ret
sigma_mam <- sd(mam_resid)
alpha_mam <- 0
beta_mam  <- 1
df_mam <- n_est - 1  # effectively estimating only variance

# (C) Provided-beta model: use given beta, estimate alpha with fixed beta on pre-window
if(length(unique(df$beta)) == 1) {
  beta_prov <- unique(df$beta)[1]
} else {
  # If beta varies (unexpected), take average in estimation window
  beta_prov <- mean(est$beta, na.rm = TRUE)
}
alpha_fixb <- mean(est$ret - beta_prov * est$mkt_ret, na.rm = TRUE)
fixb_resid <- est$ret - (alpha_fixb + beta_prov * est$mkt_ret)
sigma_fixb <- sd(fixb_resid)
df_fixb <- n_est - 1  # alpha estimated given fixed beta

# 4) Compute CARs and t-stats for each model and window
# Main model (market model)
main_car  <- car_stats(df, alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat, main_window, est_df = n_est - 2)
alt1_car  <- car_stats(df, alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat, alt_window1, est_df = n_est - 2)
alt2_car  <- car_stats(df, alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat, alt_window2, est_df = n_est - 2)
plac_car  <- car_stats(df, alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat, placebo_window, est_df = n_est - 2)

# Robustness: market-adjusted
main_car_mam <- car_stats(df, alpha_mam, beta_mam, sigma_mam, main_window, est_df = df_mam)
alt1_car_mam <- car_stats(df, alpha_mam, beta_mam, sigma_mam, alt_window1, est_df = df_mam)

# Robustness: provided-beta
main_car_fixb <- car_stats(df, alpha_fixb, beta_prov, sigma_fixb, main_window, est_df = df_fixb)
alt1_car_fixb <- car_stats(df, alpha_fixb, beta_prov, sigma_fixb, alt_window1, est_df = df_fixb)

# 5) Print results
cat("Event Study: Impact of Emissions Standard Announcement on CAR stock\n")
cat("Estimation window: event_day <=", max(est$event_day), "with", n_est, "observations\n")
cat(sprintf("Market model estimates: alpha = %.6f, beta = %.4f, sigma(eps) = %.6f\n",
            alpha_hat, beta_hat, sigma_hat))
cat("\nMain result (Market Model):\n")
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1] = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            main_car$CAR, main_car$k, main_car$t, main_car$p))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,+1]  = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            alt1_car$CAR, alt1_car$k, alt1_car$t, alt1_car$p))
cat(sprintf("  AR[0]      = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            alt2_car$CAR, alt2_car$k, alt2_car$t, alt2_car$p))

cat("\nPlacebo (pre-event) check under Market Model:\n")
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-10,-6] = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            plac_car$CAR, plac_car$k, plac_car$t, plac_car$p))

cat("\nRobustness: Market-Adjusted (alpha=0, beta=1)\n")
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1] = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            main_car_mam$CAR, main_car_mam$k, main_car_mam$t, main_car_mam$p))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,+1]  = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            alt1_car_mam$CAR, alt1_car_mam$k, alt1_car_mam$t, alt1_car_mam$p))

cat("\nRobustness: Provided-Beta Model (beta from data)\n")
cat(sprintf("  Provided beta = %.4f; estimated alpha = %.6f; sigma(eps) = %.6f\n",
            beta_prov, alpha_fixb, sigma_fixb))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[-1,+1] = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            main_car_fixb$CAR, main_car_fixb$k, main_car_fixb$t, main_car_fixb$p))
cat(sprintf("  CAR[0,+1]  = %.4f (k=%d), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            alt1_car_fixb$CAR, alt1_car_fixb$k, alt1_car_fixb$t, alt1_car_fixb$p))

# 6) Simple interpretation prompt
cat("\nInterpretation guide:\n")
cat("  Positive and significant CAR indicates the announcement increased CAR's value.\n")
cat("  Negative and significant CAR indicates value destruction.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Modestly negative CAR around the announcement (e.g., -1% to -1.5% over [-1,+1]).
- Rationale: Tighter emissions standards typically raise expected compliance and capex costs for incumbent automakers, outweighing any resolution-of-uncertainty benefits in the immediate window. If CAR is a technological leader in emissions control, effects could be closer to zero or slightly positive, but the base-case expectation is a small negative CAR.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Analyze stock returns before and after the announcement to isolate the impact of the emissions standard announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The announcement of the new emissions standard positively affects CAR's stock returns.
